entries.name: Two-qubit gate fidelity on foundry-fabricated arrays
entries.description: Single-qubit and charge-noise results on 300 mm lines are established; the limiting step is demonstrating >99% two-qubit gates at array scale on industrial processes, then holding that under tiling.
entries.falsifier: Charge noise, valley splitting, or device-to-device variability under foundry design rules prevents >99% two-qubit operation at the densities the architecture assumes

entries.name: End-to-end photon loss below the fusion-tolerance threshold
entries.description: Every headline photonic metric is conditional on detection. The architecture lives or dies on total loss — source, waveguide, switching, coupling, detector — because fusion-based correction has a hard loss budget.
entries.falsifier: Integrated system loss cannot be reduced to the fault-tolerant fusion threshold at the required component counts

entries.name: Cryogenic wiring and control density
entries.description: Every qubit needs addressability at mK temperatures. The silicon-spin answer is co-integrated cryo-CMOS control; its open question is whether hybrid quantum+classical chips tolerate the dissipated power.
entries.falsifier: Control-electronics power dissipation destroys qubit performance before the required channel density is reached

entries.name: Real-time QEC decoding classical compute
entries.description: Fault tolerance converts qubit-count races into a decoding-rate problem: the classical stack must decode syndromes faster than errors accumulate, at scale, without becoming the bottleneck nobody budgeted.
entries.falsifier: Decoding latency or power scales worse than the error-suppression gain it enables
entries.note: Cross-architecture bottleneck registered with no best-measurement bound yet — the registry holds the question open rather than inventing a leader.
